answer: We formulate a decentralized mechanism incorporating dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices, inducing a strict Nash equilibrium that deters Sybil attacks. An agent's payoff from multiplying identities is diminished as bonds forfeit at the zenith of exploitation, converging to a vertex of negative expected returns. The marble of strategic manipulation is thus rendered unattractive, as agents optimize against the punishment matrix, guaranteeing convergence to a Sybil-resistant equilibrium.
